title: The grapes
subtitle: Four grapes, many styles
objectives: Link each grape to its area

steps.title: Four grapes
steps.body: Melon de Bourgogne makes Muscadet in the Pays Nantais. Chenin Blanc dominates Anjou and Touraine whites, dry to sweet. Cabernet Franc makes most of the reds, in Chinon, Bourgueil and Saumur-Champigny. Sauvignon Blanc leads the Central Vineyards and Touraine. Others include Gamay, Pinot Noir and Grolleau.

steps.title: Every style
steps.body: The Loire makes almost every style of wine: crisp dry whites, sweet botrytised whites, light reds, rosés, including Rosé d'Anjou, and sparkling wine, Crémant de Loire and Saumur. Cool climate and high acidity link them all. Chenin Blanc alone makes dry, sweet and sparkling.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its main area.
steps.explanation: Each part of the Loire has its grape.

steps.body: Most Loire wines are named after the place, not the grape. Learn the four grapes and their areas, and the labels open up.

steps.prompt: The Loire makes only white wine.
steps.explanation: Not true. It also makes reds, rosés and sparkling wines.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Melon, Chenin, Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon lead the Loire
Each area has its own grape
